summary: Today a local special tax — a tax earmarked for a specific purpose — needs two-thirds voter approval when a city or county proposes it, but only a simple majority when citizens put it on the ballot by initiative, under a California Supreme Court ruling. Proposition 43 closes that gap: starting January 1, 2027, every new, extended, or increased local special tax would need two-thirds voter approval no matter how it reaches the ballot. It also bars local governments, including citizen initiatives, from adding property-value-based taxes beyond those the constitution already allows.
what_yes_means: A yes vote requires two-thirds voter approval for all new or increased local special taxes, including citizen-initiative taxes that today pass with a simple majority.
what_no_means: A no vote keeps the current split: two-thirds approval for special taxes proposed by local governments, simple majority for those proposed by citizen initiative.
